requirements.title: Justified ITS resource-management methodology
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall embody and document a suitable, justified methodology for assessing and improving resource management for data-intensive ITS services.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer; University assessment authority for justification.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Project 237 deliverable A formally requires investigation of a suitable methodology; rubric S-003 requires suitability reasoning and alternatives. No later source removes obligation.
acceptance_criteria: A named methodology is documented and explicitly linked to the Project 237 resource-management objectives.
Its methods, assumptions, alternatives, and suitability are justified.
The evaluation design can answer the stated resource-management questions.
requirements.evidence_required: Dissertation methodology text, traceable method/configuration artifacts, and evaluation outputs showing that the documented method was actually used.
requirements.out_of_scope: No particular algorithm, framework, cloud provider, UI, simulator, or named experiment family is mandated.
dependencies: TT-REQ-001 declaration of final specialised research question; supervisor approval incomplete — EXTERNAL DECISION REQUIRED
requirements.superseded_formulations: None found. Later specialisations may instantiate this requirement but have not replaced it.

requirements.title: Implemented ITS service use cases
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall design and implement a few ITS service use cases sufficient to exercise the selected resource-management methodology and service-quality questions.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for the obligation; MEDIUM for the minimum count and what qualifies as a distinct use case.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Project 237 deliverable B explicitly requires design and implementation of a few ITS service use cases. Later notes discuss VEC/cases but do not redefine number/identity.
acceptance_criteria: More than one clearly differentiated ITS service use case is designed and implemented; for audit purposes, the minimum operational interpretation is two while the source ambiguity around "a few" is declared.
Each use case states its service purpose, workload/input, resource needs, and relevant QoS outcomes.
Each use case has observable executable or generated behavior sufficient to support the investigation.
requirements.evidence_required: Reachable use-case entry points or reproducible executions, representative inputs, generated outputs, and tests or direct probes demonstrating behavior.
requirements.out_of_scope: The brief does not mandate Manchester, VEC, journey-time prediction, forecasting, SUMO, live data, or a digital-twin UI as the specific use cases.
dependencies: TT-REQ-001; the selected use cases must be relevant to the resource-management objectives.
requirements.superseded_formulations: No formal supersession. INFERENCE: whether variants within one VEC scenario qualify as several use cases remains open.

requirements.title: Run-time profiling of data-intensive ITS services
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall support investigation of the run-time profile of its selected data-intensive ITS service use cases, including resource behavior and service-quality outcomes relevant to the research question.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Project 237 deliverable C establishes run-time profiling. Later RSU notes suggest load/queues/latency as possible specialisations, not a fixed catalogue.
acceptance_criteria: Run-time evidence is produced for every selected use case under declared workloads/scenarios.
Resource and service-quality measures are defined with units and interpreted in relation to the research question.
The evidence distinguishes executed observations from static design descriptions.
requirements.evidence_required: Reproducible run outputs, measurements/logs or generated artifacts, configuration/workload identity, and analysis that ties observations to the named use cases.
requirements.out_of_scope: No exact metric set, instrumentation architecture, dashboard, or statistical package is mandated.

requirements.title: Assessment of existing resource-management strategies
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall support an evidence-based assessment of the suitability of existing cloud, edge, or otherwise applicable resource-management strategies for meeting the requirements and quality-of-service needs of the selected ITS services.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer.
requirements.confidence: HIGH; MEDIUM on whether later VEC/RSU work is the agreed complete instantiation.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Project 237 deliverable D explicitly requires this assessment. Edge/RSU strategies are plausible instantiation, not prescribed MAPPO/Kubernetes.
acceptance_criteria: Existing strategies or a defensibly defined strategy family are named and described.
Their suitability is evaluated against explicit ITS service and QoS criteria using common, justified evidence.
The assessment reports limitations and conditions of suitability, not merely feature descriptions or a presumed universal winner.
requirements.evidence_required: Comparative run artifacts or other justified empirical evidence, strategy configurations, QoS definitions, analysis, and conclusions traceable to the evidence.
requirements.out_of_scope: No specific algorithm, platform, number of controllers, or production cloud deployment is required.
requirements.superseded_formulations: None. The late RSU direction may specialise this requirement but does not authoritatively replace it — PROVISIONAL WORDING.

requirements.title: Improved dynamic resource-management strategy
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall support the proposal of one or more improved strategies for dynamic management of storage and/or computing resources across available devices and clouds for ITS data processing and information provision, taking relevant quality-of-service requirements into account.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as Project 237 proposer.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for the obligation; MEDIUM for the required implementation depth.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Project 237 objective and deliverable E. Later notes suggest deterministic/learned RSU load management as candidates, but minimum remains outcome-level.
acceptance_criteria: At least one improved dynamic strategy is specified clearly enough to assess or reproduce conceptually.
It responds to a limitation identified under TT-REQ-004 and explains how it manages storage and/or compute resources under mobility/dynamicity.
Its expected or observed QoS effects and trade-offs are evaluated or defensibly analysed.
requirements.evidence_required: A strategy specification, traceability to an identified deficiency, and empirical evaluation or a justified design-level analysis appropriate to the selected methodology.
requirements.out_of_scope: "Propose" does not by itself require production deployment, a novel DRL model, Kubernetes, proactive scaling, or full implementation of every proposed strategy.
requirements.superseded_formulations: None. Specific controller formulations in later notes remain specialisations or proposals — INFERENCE.

requirements.title: Goal-aligned evaluation and evidence-supported conclusions
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall be evaluated, tested, or critically reflected upon using justified methods aligned with the stated project goals, and every material conclusion shall be supported by the resulting evidence.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: University assessment authority; Dr Sandra Sampaio for project-goal alignment.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Rubric S-003 formally requires justified evaluation aligned with project goals and evidence-supported conclusions. Sandra notes reinforce credible sources and mechanism explanation.
acceptance_criteria: Objectives, evaluation questions, methods, evidence, and conclusions are traceable to one another.
Evaluation-method choices and relevant alternatives are justified.
Negative results, failures, uncertainty, confounders, and limitations are reported where material.
Conclusions do not exceed what the evidence demonstrates.
requirements.evidence_required: The dissertation/report, cited literature, evaluation plan, executed outputs, analysis, and a trace from each material conclusion to supporting evidence.
requirements.out_of_scope: No particular statistical test, seed count, user study, experiment-lane name, or requirement for a positive result is imposed.
dependencies: TT-REQ-001 and the final declared project objectives.
requirements.superseded_formulations: Detailed evidence ledgers/manifests in internal designs are implementation choices, not separately negotiated requirements.

requirements.title: Report and complementary video demonstration
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall be presented through the assessed report and a 6–8 minute video that complements the report and appropriately demonstrates or visualises completed work.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Handbook S-004 requires report/video submission; rubric S-003 fixes 6–8 minute duration and complement requirement.
acceptance_criteria: The report describes purpose, methods, results, evaluation/reflection, limitations, and conclusions.
A 6–8 minute video presents completed aspects that complement rather than merely duplicate the report.
The demonstration is aligned with the original goals and does not present proposed or unavailable behavior as completed.
requirements.evidence_required: The submitted report and timestamped video, plus any demonstration inputs/outputs needed to substantiate shown behavior.
requirements.out_of_scope: No live deployment, live SUMO execution, mobile application, public website, or real-time feed is mandated by the rubric.
dependencies: Completed work and a settled statement of project goals.

requirements.title: Comparative infrastructure-side RSU load-management investigation
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, if the late RSU research direction is confirmed, support comparison of the existing vehicle-side offloading arrangement with a deterministic/rule-based infrastructure-side load-management approach and a separately defined learned scheduling/load-management approach, identifying the operating conditions in which each approach performs better.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Reportedly Dr Sandra Sampaio for dissertation direction; Randy Prasetia Putra only for relevant technical semantics.
requirements.confidence: MEDIUM for the direction; LOW-MEDIUM for the exact comparison set and assessed priority. DIRECT_SUPERVISOR_SOURCE_BODY S-035 (SHA 08e0fedfedb44c7e9e48ba5a5faf8c6e467d670fdc9d966b7ec11c00c00492ed) raises direct source confidence but does not change SHOULD priority or silently amend the frozen requirement.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: if the late RSU research direction is confirmed
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Meeting 4 (S-012) and 4 August paraphrase (S-011) point to three-way comparison; both were Class C. DIRECT_SUPERVISOR_SOURCE_BODY S-035 (SANDRA-DIRECT-BODY-2026-08-04) verbatim body now provides direct supervisor evidence for overlapping content — RSU queue/waiting-room capacity (not compute), fail-fast accounting, no current RSU load awareness in vehicle policy, disproportionate load at congested RSUs, and three requested investigations: (A) DRL+deterministic Kubernetes load balancing, (B) DRL+DRL scheduling, (C) DRL+AI-based Kubernetes. S-035 does not establish timestamp/headers/Outlook provenance and does not make any direction a mandatory assessed implementation without additional authoritative evidence.
acceptance_criteria: The existing vehicle-side arrangement, a deterministic infrastructure approach, and a separately defined learned infrastructure approach have explicit authority boundaries and configurations.
They are compared on common resource/QoS outcomes under materially different operating conditions.
The analysis identifies conditional strengths, weaknesses, and limitations rather than claiming one universal winner.
If the source decision is not confirmed, the work explicitly presents this as an investigated option rather than a negotiated mandatory deliverable.
requirements.evidence_required: Primary supervisor confirmation or explicit caveating; executable comparison artifacts; shared scenarios and metrics; generated results; and dissertation analysis.
requirements.out_of_scope: DLA, action masking, proactive 15-second scaling, Kubernetes control, oracle baselines, RSU-load observation retraining, and every controller in later analyses are not implied.
dependencies: Retrieval or confirmation of Sandra's 4 August direction; TT-REQ-003, TT-REQ-004, TT-REQ-006, and TT-REQ-011 if Randy's environment is used.
requirements.superseded_formulations: The earlier claim that lowering a generic "capacity" produced improvement was technically corrected by S-007 and must not define this comparison.

supervisor_identified_problem: RSU queue/waiting-room capacity misidentified as compute; fail-fast accounting; lack of RSU load awareness in vehicle policy; disproportionate load at congested RSUs with idle distant RSUs; infrastructure load management as supervisor-identified problem
requested_investigation: (A) DRL offloading plus deterministic load balancing (Kubernetes)
(B) DRL offloading plus DRL scheduling/load balancing
(C) DRL offloading plus AI-based infrastructure/resource control
proposed_direction: Each of A/B/C is a proposed direction, not a mandatory assessed implementation without additional authoritative evidence
hypothesised_outcome: Improved task completion rates under combined DRL+load-balancing — hypothesised outcome, not proven

requirements.title: Varied, controlled, non-trivial comparative scenarios
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, where comparative or causal claims are made, use sufficiently varied, challenging, and controlled scenarios to expose where resource-management strategies succeed or fail and to address uncertainty or statistical validity.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio; University assessment authority.
requirements.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH for the principle; LOW for any detailed campaign specification.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: where comparative or causal claims are made
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Sandra notes reject trivial scenarios and ask for diverse conditions/seeds; rubric requires justified evaluation; Randy S-007 agrees separated changes are good practice and accepts selected controls.
acceptance_criteria: Scenarios cover materially different workload, traffic, incident, or resource conditions justified against the research question.
Material interventions are isolated or combined changes are explicitly disclosed.
Seeds, uncertainty, statistical validity, or another suitable repeatability treatment are reported.
Null, adverse, and non-obvious outcomes are retained and interpreted.
requirements.evidence_required: Predeclared or otherwise documented scenario/configuration definitions, repeatable run outputs, uncertainty/statistical analysis, and comparison tables or plots.
requirements.out_of_scope: No exact seed count, confidence threshold, scenario catalogue, tool, or E0/E1/E2/E2b/E2c/E2d sequence is negotiated.
requirements.superseded_formulations: Single trivial or causally confounded demonstrations are inconsistent with later supervisor guidance; no exact replacement protocol was formally fixed.

requirements.title: Technically accurate and honestly bounded evidence claims
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall make technically accurate, evidence-backed claims and shall explicitly distinguish observed provider data, simulated mobility, and synthetic or assumed task/RSU inputs; it shall not present a Manchester label or provider account as proof of real Manchester VEC validation.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: University assessment authority; Dr Sandra Sampaio for the mixed-real/synthetic case boundary.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for technical accuracy and evidence-bounded claims; MEDIUM for the exact Manchester dataset Sandra intended.
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Rubric S-003 assesses technical accuracy; S-011 says traffic data may ground mobility while task/RSU still fabricated (mixed/synthetic boundary); provider records prove access conditions, not delivered measured data; Randy S-007 confirms experimental scaling conventions are not physical claims.
acceptance_criteria: Every material dataset/input and output is labelled as observed, simulated, synthetic, mixed, or unavailable with its provenance.
Claims such as "live," "current," "real Manchester," and "validated" do not exceed the demonstrated evidence layer.
Provider activation/request/availability is not described as data delivery or integration without direct evidence.
Limitations and unavailable evidence are explicit in product-facing outputs and dissertation claims where relevant.
requirements.evidence_required: Dataset provenance and standing, source identifiers, product/report labels, representative outputs, and a claim-to-evidence review.
requirements.out_of_scope: This requirement does not mandate real Manchester data, a live feed, or a particular provenance UI.
dependencies: Applies whenever data, geography, realism, validation, or experimental results are claimed.
requirements.superseded_formulations: "Real-world validation" inferred solely from Manchester/Etihad/Co-op Live naming, or from provider access, is superseded by the mixed/synthetic boundary recorded in S-011 and the actual access standing in S-005/S-006.

requirements.title: Correct RSU admission and compute semantics
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, whenever it uses Randy's environment or results, distinguish the per-RSU admission/in-flight waiting-room ceiling from compute service rate or worker capacity, preserve terminal rejection of surplus tasks outside the RSU queue, and avoid describing an admission-limit change as a processing-capacity change.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Randy Prasetia Putra as technical producer; reportedly adopted by Dr Sandra Sampaio.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for technical semantics; MEDIUM for supervisor adoption.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: whenever it uses Randy's environment or results
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Randy S-007 directly confirms per-RSU admission/in-flight ceiling unrelated to processing power, immediate terminal rejection with no retry/fallback/re-forwarding, and that rejected work never enters queue.
acceptance_criteria: Definitions, configuration names, units, UI/report text, and analysis keep admission limit separate from compute/service capacity.
Surplus tasks are rejected immediately and never enter an RSU queue in any claimed reproduction of Randy's semantics.
Prior or current findings do not attribute an admission-clamp effect to compute scaling.
Any alternative semantics are explicitly labelled as a new model, not Randy's confirmed environment.
requirements.evidence_required: Configuration/schema definitions, public/report terminology, targeted boundary probes, queue/rejection traces, and corrected analysis of affected experiments.
requirements.out_of_scope: Per-task ledger fields, two-population reporting, action masking, exact backhaul, staleness sweeps, proactive scaling, and DLA are not required merely because Randy suggested them.
dependencies: Triggered only if Randy's environment, data, or reported results are used or reproduced.
requirements.superseded_formulations: RSU_MAX_CONCURRENT interpreted as processing capacity, and the generic "3.3 times capacity reduction" interpretation, are superseded by S-007's direct correction.

requirements.title: Provider access, provenance, and attribution compliance
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, whenever National Highways or TfGM information is used, follow the applicable granted access path and licence conditions, retain sufficient source/time metadata for defensible interpretation, and provide the required source acknowledgement.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: National Highways and Transport for Greater Manchester as data providers.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for the known terms; LOW for TfGM delivery because the necessary follow-up is not accessible.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: whenever National Highways or TfGM information is used
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: National Highways S-005 granted portal access under attribution licence; TfGM S-006 confirmed possible availability, requested acknowledgement, required academic-email/tutor-copy before details.
acceptance_criteria: For every used provider dataset, a retrievable licence/access basis, source identity, relevant time-zone/metadata interpretation, and required acknowledgement are recorded.
National Highways information carries its required attribution.
A TfGM access/delivery claim is made only if the academic-email/tutor-copy condition and any subsequently agreed access conditions are evidenced.
Credentials or restricted provider material are not exposed as public evidence.
requirements.evidence_required: Provider licence/access correspondence, dataset identity and metadata, displayed/published attribution, and evidence of compliance with any delivery-specific terms.
requirements.out_of_scope: This requirement does not require either provider to be used and does not treat portal activation or favourable correspondence as successful integration.
dependencies: Triggered only when National Highways or TfGM information is used or claimed.
requirements.superseded_formulations: The student requests' desired field lists do not become provider-accepted requirements. Portal activation does not satisfy the unresponded measured-data request.

requirements.title: Ethics and information-governance gate
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, before any work involving human participants, human issues, or personal data begins, obtain the applicable University ethics approval or confirmed exemption and follow relevant information-governance policy.
requirements.confidence: HIGH for the conditional rule; LOW on whether the contemplated evaluation triggers it.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: before any work involving human participants, human issues, or personal data begins
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: University guidance S-002/S-004 makes approval/exemption mandatory before covered activity; Meeting 2 S-009 raises possible user evaluation; S-023 shows formal vs informal evaluation route never settled.
acceptance_criteria: Either no covered activity occurred, with the data/evaluation boundary documented, or a dated approval/exemption predates recruitment or covered data collection.
Conduct and data handling follow the approved/exempt route.
requirements.evidence_required: An approval/exemption record and protocol, or a documented demonstration that no human-participant/human-issue/personal-data activity was performed.
requirements.out_of_scope: This requirement does not itself mandate a user study and does not presume that wholly synthetic or open non-personal data requires participant ethics approval.
dependencies: Triggered only by covered participant or data activity.
requirements.superseded_formulations: No formal or informal user-evaluation route has been accepted in the accessible sources.

requirements.title: Small TrafficTwin data-engineering and what-if extension
requirements.canonical_quotation: TrafficTwin shall, if selected after completion of the core scientific work and if time permits, provide a small data-engineering extension that demonstrates a bounded path from honestly identified traffic inputs through retained context and analysis or prediction to a user-defined what-if scenario and decision-support output, using simulation where appropriate.
requirements.primary_stakeholder: Dr Sandra Sampaio as proposer of the optional extension; Abdulla as product owner choosing whether to pursue it.
requirements.confidence: HIGH that the latest accessible platform-specific supervisor note makes this optional; MEDIUM on whether unseen later correspondence changed that priority.
requirements.conditional_trigger_text: if selected after completion of the core scientific work and if time permits
requirements.negotiation_history_summary: SOURCE-DERIVED FACT: Meeting 1 S-008 calls platform a possibility; Meeting 2 S-009 expands to possible Manchester app but leaves choice open; Meeting 3 S-010 demotes to small extension after main work, if time remains; later owner designs S-021/S-022 lack supervisor sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Only if claimed as delivered, one bounded end-to-end workflow connects declared inputs, retained context, analysis/prediction or scenario processing, and an inspectable decision-support output.
Each step is reachable and behaviorally demonstrated rather than represented by names, screens, or documents alone.
Data and simulation standing complies with TT-REQ-010.
The selected subset and omitted elements are explicit; the full vision is not presumed.
requirements.evidence_required: A reachable product workflow, representative input, generated output, tests/direct probes, and honest evidence-standing labels.
requirements.out_of_scope: A production digital twin, complete heterogeneous live ingestion, live Manchester feed, automatic decision execution, mobile app, required forecasting model, or mandatory SUMO product path is not implied.
dependencies: Completion of the core scientific work; TT-REQ-010 and TT-REQ-012 if provider data is used.
requirements.superseded_formulations: Any reading of Meetings 1–2 or owner designs that makes the full platform the agreed assessed core is superseded by Meeting 3's explicit "extension" / "if you have time" wording, subject to recovery of later primary evidence — INFERENCE until primary email recovered.
